        The Atlanta Dream took a 2-1 lead over the Golden State Valkyries in the WNBA Finals with a Game 3 win on Wednesday night. Angel Reese scored a game-high 21 points in the win and was one of five Dream players to score in double figures. The series resumes on Saturday in Atlanta as the Dream host Game 4. Both teams are looking to win a title for the first time in franchise history.The Dream and Valkyries both completed semifinal sweeps, giving them a week off before the Finals. Atlanta knocked out the New York Liberty, while Golden State ousted the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces. The Dream knocked the Washington Mystics out in the first round and are a perfect 5-0 in the playoffs. The Valkyries defeated the Dallas Wings in the first round, needing all three games to do so. The Finals, for the second season ever, are a best-of-seven series in 2026.The 2026 WNBA season has been groundbreaking, on and off the court. It launched on the heels of a contentious and extended labor battle that resulted in a historic raise for the players (the salary cap increased from $1.5 million in 2025 to $7 million in 2026), and in return, the players raised the bar on a weekly basis. How to bet on horse racing: Most popular types of wagers     There are a plethora of different wagering options available on each race. We will go through the three traditional bets – Win, Place and Show – as well as the combinations of each. Below are horse racing betting tips that identify bet types and the differences between the odds found at sportsbook and racing odds.Each horse will have different odds for each bet type. These odds let you know the horse's expected return on each individual bet type. It's important to note that the odds on each horse fluctuate constantly and payouts are calculated based on the final odds, not the exact odds from the time you place your bet, a major difference from betting on other sports.           Differences in horse racing odds vs. sportsbook odds           Horse racing odds rely on pari-mutuel wagering, which is a system that pools together all of the money bet on each market up until the race begins. The track and the books take a certain percentage or rake for their operations (the Takeout), and the remainder of the pool is then divided among the winning ticket holders. The takeout is divided between the house (track) and horsemen, including race purses.             What is particularly unique about this system for those who are accustomed to betting on sports is that your odds can shift after you place the bet until they lock when the race begins. On sports betting apps, if you bet something at 10-1 and it later moves to 8-1, you still receive the 10-1 payout. In horse racing, your payout will change based on the way the market moves to create the final odds. The final odds you'll receive are determined by how much is bet on each horse and the Takeout.            The standard horse racing unit for win, place, or show bets is $2.                     Win           The win bet is simply betting on which horse will come in first place. Using the 2026 Herbie Dyke Stakes as an example, the winner was Legarto and finished with 12-5 odds. A $2 Win bet paid $6.80, a product of the standard $4.80 for a 12-5 payout on a $2 bet, plus your original $2 wager amount back.                      Place           The Place bet allows you to wager on whether a horse will finish first or second in a race, meaning two Place bets will pay out on each race. This gives you a greater chance of winning, but lowers your odds on the horse if they place.            Using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as the example again, a $2 Place bet on the No. 18 horse only returned $7.50 compared to the $17.96 for a Win bet. But also, a $2 Place bet on the No. 8 horse (Journalism), who was the favorite but came in second, paid $4.94 while the Win bet lost.                       Show           A Show bet is a highly conservative betting option. You are wagering on whether a horse will finish in the top three positions. That means three Show bets will pay out each race. For example, a $2 Show bet on a 10-1 winner returned $4. As one might expect, show bet odds are far less favorable than win bet odds, making them one of the more conservative wagers available in horse racing.                       Win/Place           Additionally, you can combine these bets on each horse when you're placing your wagers. That means if you want to bet on a horse to win and place, you can do that. A $2 Win/Place bet really means you're betting $4 – a $2 Win bet and a $2 Place bet. If the horse you bet on wins, you will win both bets. If the horse finishes second, you would only win the Place bet.                       Place/Show           The same is available for a Place/Show bet, where a $2 Place/Show bet would be $4 wagered on a $2 Place bet and a $2 Show bet. If your horse finishes first or second, you would win both, but if it finishes third, you would only win the Show bet.                       Win/Place/Show (Across The Board)            Lastly, you can bet on all three options in what is often referred to as an Across The Board bet. A $2 Across The Board bet would really be $6 wagered – $2 on Win, $2 on Place, and $2 on Show. If you make an Across The Board bet and your horse wins, you pay out on all three wagers.            It's important to note that betting on Win/Place/Show combinations may not result in a net return even if one of the bets pays. For example, at the 2024 Kentucky Derby, an Across The Board bet on the 11 horse would've returned just $5.58 on $6 wagered.                       The most popular horse racing bet types           Many horse racing bettors place exotic bets to try to predict where multiple horses will finish in a race. These combination wagers offer the chance for bigger payouts, but come with a lower probability of winning (just like same game parlays in sports betting).            It is important to note that, unlike sports betting, there is no standard odds calculation to use for determining exotic payouts. Because of parimutuel wagering, odds can fluctuate until the race begins based on which horses are taking the most action. Additionally, live horse racing betting is available, adding another layer of entertainment for those watching races as they take place.           Exactas           An exacta bet in horse racing functions the same as it does across other sports. The bettor must pick the exact finishing order. For example, if someone wants to place an exacta bet with two horses, they must select each horse and where it will finish exactly. Once again using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as an example, a $2 exacta on the No. 18 and No. 8 horses (who closed with final odds of 7-1 and almost 3-1) paid $48.32. This style of betting can be seen in plenty of other sports, especially in futures betting.Exotics winnings will vary based on the number of horses in the race, the odds of the top-finishing horses, and the size of the pool. For example, the field for the 2024 Kentucky Derby saw a longer shot horse win, so the exacta pool paid $258.56 -- significantly more than the 2025 Derby.                       Trifectas           This horse racing wager is placing a bet on the exact order of the top-three finishers in a race. A straight trifecta will pay handsomely, but is extremely difficult to hit. Trifecta payouts are often shown for $0.50 bets, but some will show for $1 bets as well. The payout screen will tell you which, but that's important to note so you're aware of how much you are getting back.            The 2025 Kentucky Derby Trifecta paid $231.12 on a $1 Trifecta bet.                       Superfectas           Superfecta bets try to predict the exact order of the top-four finishers in a horse race. The superfecta payout is usually shown for a $1 bet. For the 2025 Kentucky Derby, a $1 superfecta that added the fourth-place No. 3 horse to the trifecta paid $1,682.27.                      Super High 5           Some books will allow you to bet on the top-five finishers in their exact order in what is called a Super High 5 bet. Those payouts will again be shown for a $1 wager. The odds of hitting a Super High 5, especially in a large field race, are exceptionally low. They are equivalent to multi-leg futures parlays in sports betting.The 2025 Kentucky Derby's $1 Super High Five paid $38,405.96.                      Box           A box bet allows you to have every possible combination for exotics. If you think you know which two horses will hit the exacta but are not sure of their specific order, you can box it. The same goes for trifectas and superfectas. The more horses you box together, the lower your total profits on the payout will be.            For example, a three-horse exacta box bet costs $12 to bet, as you are betting $2 on all six potential combinations between those three horses:           $2 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 3 second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 1 in first and No. 3 in secondYou can do the same for Trifectas and Superfectas, but at exponentially escalating costs. A $1 Trifecta Box with three horses is six combinations, so $6 wagered:           $1 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 1 in first, No. 3 in second, No. 2 in first$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 2 in third$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 1 in firstFrom there, four horses in a $1 trifecta box is 24 combinations for $24 wagered. Five horses make 60 possible combinations for $60.            A $1 Superfecta box of four horses is $24 wagered, five horses is $120 wagered and six horses is $360 wagered.                       How to bet on horse racing: Multi-race wagers           While those exotics offer a variety of options for betting on individual races, you can also bet on multiple races at the same track in various ways. These combination wagers pay out based on the betting pool, allowing you to choose a handful of horses you're confident in throughout the day to increase your potential payout.                       Daily Double           The Daily Double is exactly what it sounds like: Betting on back-to-back race winners from that day. The odds for Daily Doubles vary based on the odds for the individual horses you bet and the overall Daily Double betting pool. As an example, the $2 Daily Double at Horseshoe Indianapolis on April 15, 2025 from the first two races with the 7 horse in the first race (went off at 1-1 odds) and the 4 horse in the second race (went off at 3-5 odds) paid $8.            Once the first race ends, the payouts for each potential Daily Double will be shown under a "Will Pays" tab on the next race's betting screen.                       Pick-3, Pick-4, Pick-5 and Pick-6           Along with the Daily Double, there are more options for betting the winner of multiple races in a row at the same track. The Pick-3 is picking the winner in three consecutive races, the Pick-4 in four consecutive races, and so on for the Pick-5 and Pick-6.           Like exotics, the pool amount and the odds for each horse wagered on determine the payouts for these multi-race wagers. The default unit for these bets varies from book to book, with FanDuel showing $0.50 payouts and TwinSpires showing $1 payouts in the Will Pays section.            The more races you put together on a ticket, the more you can win. But as with any multi-race wager, the more legs you add, the harder it is to win. In this way, these bets function similarly to parlays in other sports.For some of the biggest races, the Pick-6 will feature a set guaranteed prize pool for the winner(s) no matter what the actual wagered amount is. The 2024 Kentucky Derby featured a $1 million guaranteed pool on TwinSpires for Pick-6s on races 6 through 11 at Churchill Downs.                       Understanding horse racing payouts           After the race, the winning payouts will be displayed for each bet type. The standard unit for win/place/show and exactas is a $2 bet. Trifectas, superfectas and super high 5s are typically shown as $1 or $0.50, but will say explicitly which on the payout board.            The payouts for each horse in the top three for the 2025 Kentucky Derby looked as follows:           2025 Kentucky DerbyWinPlaceShowSovereignty (No. 18) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$17.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$7.50 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$5.58 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Journalism (No. 8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								           $4.94 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$3.70 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Baeza (No. 21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								           				           $8.38 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				           If you bet more (or less) than the standard $2 unit, you multiply the payout by how much you bet and divide by the standard unit. For example, a $10 Win bet on Sovereignty returned $89.80, while a $25 Show bet on Journalism would've returned $46.25.            For the single-race exotics at the 2025 Kentucky Derby, the payouts were as follows:            2025 Kentucky DerbyPayout$2 Exacta (18-8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$48.32 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Trifecta (18-8-21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$231.12 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Superfecta (18-8-21-3) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1,682.27 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Super High 5 (18-8-21-3-20) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$38,405.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				          Biggest horse races beyond Kentucky Derby betting          The horse racing calendar operates year-round, but there are six events on the schedule that serve as the most important, thus attracting the best fields. The three Triple Crown events headline for the general public, but the Breeders' Cup, Pegasus World Cup and Dubai World Cup all offer massive purses and attract some of the best horses and fields in all of racing.           October 30-31, 2026: Breeders' Cup January 23, 2027: Pegasus World CupMarch 27, 2027: Dubai World CupMay 1, 2027: Kentucky DerbyMay 15, 2027: Preakness StakesJune 5, 2027: Belmont Stakes           Triple Crown of horse racing           The Kentucky Derby, Preakness Stakes and Belmont Stakes make up horse racing's Triple Crown. There are 13 horses that have completed the Triple Crown, winning all three events, and only two – American Pharoah (2015) and Justify (2018) – have accomplished that feat in the 21st century.            Not every horse competes in all three Triple Crown events. Each race operates at different lengths, and the turnaround time can be too quick for trainers to be comfortable running their horse in one after the other. Some Derby winners don't run the Preakness, while some have made it two legs before withdrawing from the Belmont.            The Kentucky Derby is a 1 1/4 mile race, the Preakness Stakes is 1 3/16 mile, and the Belmont Stakes is a grueling 1 1/2 mile event (although it is being run currently at 1 1/4 mile at Saratoga Race Course due to renovations at Belmont Park).                       Tips and advice for betting on horse racing           There are a number of strategies for betting on horse racing, but it all starts with understanding the horses and knowing their strengths, weaknesses and past performances.                       Racing forms and past performances           Racing forms are race-day publications and programs available at tracks and online to preview the day's races at each track. They are full of data and information from past races. All of the best horse racing betting apps have integrated much of this information into their betting screen.                       Track conditions           Before you even get to the horses, understanding track conditions is vital. Knowing if a track is dirt or grass, firm and fast or soft and slow, is critical information to know so you can look at which horses in a given race run best in certain conditions.                       Horse tendencies            From there, you want to understand the tendencies of horses in the field. Some horses get out to fast starts and try to push the pace, while others hang back and try to make a late kick. If most of the field is expected to push the pace and run it fast, then a horse that prefers to stay back may be at an advantage due to its advantage in a late-game run.            The opposite could be true, too; if the pace is going to be slower early, frontrunners are more likely to hold their position. Some of this information can be found in PPs or Past Performance data.                       Post position           Post position can also matter to a horse's success. Some prefer to run the rail (on the inside of the track) while others prefer being on the outside and running with more space around them. This information is all worth considering and comparing with the other horses in the field.                      Trainer and jockey information           A horse's trainer and jockey will also have tendencies. Some trainers are better at getting horses ready for a certain type of track, but maybe don't have a great track record at others. Some jockeys may be more or less aggressive on the track, which may or may not work well with that specific horse's tendencies, or they may have a long track record with that horse and know how to get the most out of them.                       Workout times           There's also plenty of data available that can help you. Workout times, if available, can give you an idea of how a horse has been running in training before a big race.                       Speed figures           Speed figures are like advanced stats of the horse racing world, offering a metric to show how well a horse has been running in its recent races that factors in things like field strength and track quality.            Taking all of that data into account is important to betting on horse racing, and for beginners it's best to ease in and do as much observing as you do betting. You'll start to find certain trends for horses, jockeys, trainers and tracks that can help you find edges on the odds board going forward.                      Manage your horse racing betting bankroll           Managing your bankroll with what percentage of money you have set aside for horse racing betting is vital to increasing your chances of scoring big at some point. Just like in sports betting, where most bankroll management experts advise no more than 2% of your bankroll should be bet on any given game, the same principle can be applied to any given horse race.                       Rules and responsible gaming           Responsible gambling is taken very seriously across all racebooks. All provide the necessary resources and contact information if you or someone you know may have a gambling problem. The minimum age is 18 for horse racing betting in most states, but it is 21 in some states.           Responsible gambling resources include the National Council for Problem Gambling (NCPG) and Gamblers Anonymous. Be smart. Bet smart. Wager responsibly. Those in need of help can also call or text 1-800-GAMBLER (1-800-426-2537). Help is available 24 hours a day and seven days a week.           FAQHow to bet on horse racing?There are several ways to bet on horse racing. The most common methods are through horse racing betting apps like TwinSpires, FanDuel Racing, and DraftKings Horse. Users can bet on a variety of outcomes, with the most common wager coming on which horse will win the given race outright.How to bet on horse racing online?Online horse racing betting is widely accessible. TwinSpires, DraftKings Horse, and FanDuel Racing all provide users with a huge array of betting options on all major races.What is a box bet in horse racing?A box bet in horse racing involves picking the finishing order of the horses. Wagerers can choose the order of the first two, three, four, or five finishers, with the return on their bet increasing with every additional horse they include in their wager. If a bettor chooses three horses for a box bet, they do not need to finish in an exact order. If they make up the top three, the bet is successful.What is a show bet in horse racing?A show bet is a wager on a specific horse to finish among the top three horses in a given race. Show bets are extremely common wagers that offer less risk and smaller payouts.What is a key box bet in horse racing?A key box bet, unsurprisingly, functions similarly to a box bet. A bettor can select a "key" horse that they believe will finish in an exact position while rounding out the rest of the box in the same fashion as a regular box bet. For example, a bettor could select Horse A to finish first while picking Horses C, B, and D to round out the top four. However, if Horse A does not finish first, the bet loses.

        Opening night is here, and the fantasy basketball injury report is already crowded. Bradley Beal, Brandon Ingram, Ben Simmons, Jimmy Butler, Mark Williams and Shaedon Sharpe headline a long list of key players who are sidelined, and each absence changes fantasy value for their teammates. Rookie Keaton Wagler is in line for a starting role with the Clippers, while Jaxson Hayes, Jalen Smith, Derrick Jones and Dennis Schroder could all see bigger workloads. Use this guide for the latest NBA injury news, expected return timelines, and the best waiver wire pickups, sleepers and streaming options to protect your fantasy basketball roster in 2026-27.Bradley Beal, Max Strus, Brandon Ingram ClippersBeal is listed as out, with knee inflammation and has no solid return date confirmed. Strus is dealing with a partial tear to his plantar fascia, an injury that will keep him out for at least the first couple of weeks of the season. Ingram was on track to carry a major offensive load when he was traded over from the Raptors late in the offseason. However, it was discovered that he had a partially torn Achilles, which has since been addressed through surgery, resulting in an uncertain return date for the 29-year-old. 
On the flip side, fifth-overall pick Keaton Wagler is projected to gain a significant boost and start at shooting guard. The handful of injuries to wing players puts the rookie in line for a great opportunity to get his NBA career off to a hot start. Additionally, Kris Dunn, Kobe Sanders and Gradey Dick are also likely to see more action while Beal and Strus remain sidelined. Derrick Jones will be the one to step up in the absence of Ingram. Jones has proven that he can provide good value as a starter and should serve as a reliable replacement. Jusuf Nurkic, Kyle Filipowski, Jazz Nurkic is expected to be sidelined until at least early November due to a partial plantar plate tear in his toe. Filipowski is sidelined due to ongoing recovery from a back surgery and is without a clear timeline for return. In the meantime, Jaxson Hayes is up for a significant role, as he is likely to start at center, while Mo Bamba is in line as a backup. Ace Bailey and Brice Sensabaugh could also see a boost by shifting to play some minutes at power forward.  
Nic Claxton, BullsClaxton is expected to remain out for at least two weeks due to a hamstring injury. Jalen Smith is in line to handle the starting center job until Claxton's return. Patrick Williams and Zach Collins are also likely to see extra action. Ben Simmons, Maxime Raynaud, Dylan Cardwell KingsSimmons was less than a week away from a return to NBA action before he suffered a torn Achilles at practice last Sunday. He will be out for the season. 
De'Andre Hunter, Nique Clifford and Precious Achiuwa are all in place to take on more significant roles, as Simmons was initially expected to handle a heavy workload. The Kings are further shorthanded in the frontcourt, as both Raynaud (knee) and Cardwell (calf) are expected to miss a couple of weeks. Their absences open up a greater need for Achiuwa to step up, while new addition Jonathan Mogbo could also have a chance to make an impression. Mark Williams, SunsWilliams is expected to remain out for a few months as he recovers from surgery on a torn labrum in his shoulder. In his absence, the Suns will look to third-year big man Oso Ighodaro, as well as sophomore Khaman Maluach, to handle most of the work in the middle. 
Donte DiVincenzo, TimberwolvesDiVincenzo tore his Achilles tendon in the playoffs last season and is expected to remain out for most of the 2026-27 campaign. In his absence, Terrence Shannon, Isaiah Evans, Bones Hyland, and Ayo Dosunmu should all be in line to pull some extra weight. Shaedon Sharpe, Trail BlazersSharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee during the offseason and will be out until at least March 2027. The Trail Blazers have an abundance of depth on the wing, and guys like Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, and Vit Krejci are likely to be first up to receive added responsibility. Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody, Kristaps Porzingis, WarriorsButler is dealing with a knee injury and will be out until early in the new year. Moody is also dealing with a knee issue but could be back sometime in December. On the other hand, Porzingis continues to be hampered by illness and has no timeline for return. 
To compensate, the Warriors will look to Gui Santos and Yaxel Lendeborg to take on starting roles. Additionally, Draymond Green is slated to slide over to center, backed up by Al Horford. Georges Niang will also be a critical contributor off the bench for the shorthanded frontcourt. Dereck Lively, MavericksLively seems to still be on the mend from foot surgery last December. Until he returns to full steam, Daniel Gafford will be on the hook for the lion's share of work at center. Additionally, Moussa Cisse proved last season that he can step in and provide strong minutes, giving the Mavs a solid two-man rotation in the middle. Coby White, Kon Knueppel, HornetsWhite suffered a calf strain during training camp and will miss at least the season opener. Knueppel did not play during the preseason and remains on the mend with a hamstring injury but is also not expected to miss too much time. Nonetheless, it would not be surprising to see the squad exercise extra caution and patience as they bring the two young stars back into action. 
New addition Dennis Schroder is set to take over the starting job at point guard for as long as necessary. Meanwhile, Grayson Allen, Sion James and Royce O'Neale could each make a case to start at shooting guard, and all three will be critical in helping handle the bulk of work in the backcourt.

        Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom claims he was denied entry into Game 3 of the WNBA Finals between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries on Wednesday night. Freedom posted a video on social media after he declined to sit in a private suite offered to him by the Dream and State Farm Arena after he raised concerns about his safety."Enes Kanter Freedom has contacted federal, state and local authorities, the WNBA, the Atlanta Dream and State Farm Arena officials to express concerns about his personal safety during his planned attendance at Game 3 of the WNBA Finals tonight," State Farm Arena said in a statement before Wednesday's game. "The safety and security of our guests and team members is our highest priority.""Following consultations with the WNBA, Dream ownership, State Farm Arena leadership and security officials, we have directed Mr. Freedom to watch tonight's game from a private luxury suite. This arrangement is intended to address his security concerns and help provide a safe and positive experience for him and other guests. The suite will have additional security and will be his designated viewing location for the game. State police have also assigned an officer to Mr. Freedom at his request."In a video posted to social media prior to tip-off, Freedom claimed that arena security was "banning us from our purchased seats." A State Farm Arena public relations official, per ESPN, said Freedom "was offered the suite for his safety and he rejected it."
"I just got kicked out of a WNBA game for the second time in a row for supporting WOMEN!" Freedom wrote. 
        
            
                Chicago Sky owner responds to Enes Kanter Freedom's free speech lawsuit: 'Meritless and frivolous'
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Freedom, who played in the NBA from 2011-22, has spent months proclaiming to be eligible for the 2027 WNBA Draft along with fellow former NBA player Royce White, and using social media to become part of the conversation around transgender athletes. The WNBA became a battleground for the debate after comments by Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham. Freedom and White both claim to identify as women.In August, Freedom was ejected from a Chicago Sky vs. Indiana Fever game after getting into a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud. He was subsequently banned from Wintrust Arena indefinitely by Sky ownership, but the WNBA did not issue a league-wide ban. 
Earlier this week, WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert sent a letter to U.S. Rep. Marlin A. Stutzman of Indiana, in which she responded to an inquiry Stutzman and several other representatives sent regarding WNBA eligibility. "With respect to your questions regarding eligibility, only women are eligible to play in the WNBA and the individuals you cite in your letter are both men," Engelbert wrote, referring to Freedom and White.

body:
Backup keeper Ben Lundt saved the opening penalty in the shootout after Roman Burki was hospitalized, and St. Louis City SC claimed the first trophy in club history
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:52 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It took over two hours of play and a penalty shootout for St. Louis City SC to win their first trophy in club history, defeating the Columbus Crew 5-3 on Wednesday in the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup final. For the first time in 11 years, an Open Cup final was decided via a penalty shootout, and it came after St. Louis' starting keeper, Roman Burki, had to be taken to the hospital after being kneed in the head in the 78th minute of play.Benjamin Lundt came in for Burki, making his fourth appearance of the season and his second in relief of Burki in an Open Cup penalty shootout. He only saved the first penalty by Santi Rodriguez, but that would be more than enough for St. Louis to get the job done. Their takers were clinical under pressure, as midfielder Daniel Edelman went down the middle to seal the win after playing all 120-plus minutes."It's just the next guy up. Roman was a hero. He had another save in the first half, and he's throwing his body on the line there. He's done it in Europe, and he's playing here now in MLS, and he's still doing what he did in Europe," Edelman said after the game to CBS Sports, praising his keepers following the match. "It's phenomenal for him and Ben. He started it for us in the Open Cup and had a big penalty save against Houston, and he did it here again today."During the trophy lift, the team had Berki's jersey on display since he was at the hospital to be checked out. He was conscious and able to move while leaving the stadium, but it's never a good moment when a player has to be stretchered off, especially in a final, but his team managed to pull it off for him, adding to the Gateway to the West's rich history.
The city of St. Louis is no stranger to winning this competition, so it's only fitting that the first trophy in the history of the MLS club, which began play in 2023, is the U.S. Open Cup. Between 1920 and 1988, the city of St. Louis won the Open Cup 10 times, with the Busch Seniors being the most recent to win in 1988 before St. Louis City SC ended the drought. Edelman summed up what it meant to everyone."It's the first trophy for me and for a lot of guys in this city because you look up there and you see that [the support from away fans] and they completely deserve to have some silverware and for us as a team, what we've been through this year, it's phenomenal for us to have this night and have this trophy," he said.Speaking to members of that '88 team, there were times that they didn't think that St. Louis would see another U.S. Open Cup title, but under Yoann Damet, this team has come together in a big way, and being able to overcome injuries to secure the Open Cup title with their backup keeper is another way that they've showcased their resilience. Heading into the weekend, St. Louis had a 21-game unbeaten run snapped, and there was no issue being able to regain focus in this critical moment.
Columbus dominated the chances for much of the game, taking 16 shots, but only three tested the St. Louis keepers as their defense bent but didn't break. This is preparation at its finest, but this team also isn't done. Damet wants to make sure to enjoy this trophy, but doing the double is the next goal as they've risen to second in the Western Conference. This is a team that will want to win the MLS Cup and secure the league title, and Damet made sure to acknowledge that."You always want to fill the trophy cabinet, and it takes time. Success is not built overnight, so we started the team thinking, let's implement a clear vision and a clear identity of how we want to do things, and see how far we can go in year one," Damet told CBS Sports. "This is still phase one of what we're gonna be, so I'm very happy with what we've been able to do. Our consistency in the league and winning a trophy is an amazing testament to the work of the guys. At the same time, it means so much for the city and for the community, and I'm so happy."If this is only phase one with a 36-year-old coach at the helm who is also being backed by the front office, MLS may be hearing more from this club before long.

title: Grading season debuts for Giannis Antetokounmpo, Kawhi Leonard, other NBA stars - CBS Sports
description: As Giannis debuted for Miami and Kawhi made his great escape to Toronto, LaMelo Ball was up to his old tricks and
body:
As Giannis debuted for Miami and Kawhi made his great escape to Toronto, LaMelo Ball was up to his old tricks and Anthony Davis... finally played a game!
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:30 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After three games on Tuesday night, the rest of the NBA teams opened their 2026-27 seasons on Wednesday night. And with it, we finally got a look at a host of star players with their new teams in regular-season action on the heels of a rather eventful summer across the league. After grading LeBron James's opening act with the 76ers, here are the report cards for some other notables after their first games in different digs. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Giannis Antetokounmpo: B-The biggest name to change teams this offseason (non-LeBron division). Once again, Pat Riley got his man. But even after acquiring Antetokounmpo, Riley hinted that they were still looking to add another major piece, indicating that the Heat needed to improve a roster that could clearly use more floor spacing, shot creators, scoring and depth. That's certainly how it looked in the Heat's ugly 25-point home loss to the Timberwolves in the season opener. Antetokounmpo had 35 points in 30 minutes, but that still wasn't enough to keep the Heat in the game. To the extent that there were any positives for Miami, at least Giannis looked like Giannis -- including airballing a free throw and being a problem in the open court (especially when the refs were lenient with traveling violations; more on that in a moment when we get to LaMelo Ball's debut).
Antetokounmpo played just 36 games in his final season with the Bucks, the result of a combination of injuries and a late-season tank job. But prior to that, he finished in the top five in the MVP voting in seven straight seasons. He'll be 32 in December, but the Heat are betting he's healthy and has plenty of top-tier basketball still to offer. They'll need all the heavy lifting he can muster if Miami wants to join the contenders in the loaded Eastern Conference. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    LaMelo Ball: CThe "C" stands for comedy. Look, there's no denying that Ball is a skilled basketball player. In an easy win over the Heat, Ball had 21 points (on 7-for-17 shooting, including 5-for-13 from deep) and six assists. 
He looked comfortable next to Anthony Edwards, who went off for a game-high 45 points without breaking much of a sweat. Ball can hit shots from all over the court and he's a fantastic passer. But there's also a reason why the Hornets moved on from Ball, and they were right to do so. During his time in Charlotte, he demonstrated tantalizing talent, but that often came in the service of individual highlights and at the expense of team success. And while he made jaw-dropping plays with the Hornets, he also frequently left you scratching your head. About that last part, just look at this. What are we doing here?
It's not so much that Ball took, oh, all the steps after his gather in what was pretty plainly an egregious travel that went uncalled. It's more that he couldn't help laughing about it and pointing to the crowd afterward, as though he'd just drained an impressive bucket. With Ball, it's impossible to be sure if he's in on the joke or completely unaware that he's doing a bit at all times. The thinking on acquiring Ball and playing him with Edwards seems to be something on the order of the Wolves weren't going to get past the Thunder and Spurs as previously constituted, so why not give this experiment a chance? That's a hot take to be sure. Now we'll see whether the Wolves can handle it or if they eventually get burned. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kawhi Leonard: B+Following what we'll charitably label an eventful final year in Los Angeles, Leonard is back in Toronto. He's an instant upgrade over Brandon Ingram at both ends of the floor, and when paired with Scottie Barnes, the Raptors now boast two of the best two-way wings in the league. His first game back with his old club didn't put too much of a strain on Leonard. He should thank the Bulls for not putting up too many roadblocks for his reentry. In a blowout 135-92 home win, Leonard had 23 points, six rebounds, two assists, four steals and a block in just 24 minutes. He shot only 5-for-17 from the floor but made all 11 of his free throws. He was also indirectly responsible for the highlight of the night. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Anthony Davis: ARemember him? After being traded from the Lakers back in February 2025, Davis has played just 29 games -- all of them in Dallas. When the Mavericks flipped him to the Wizards last season, Davis was true to his nickname and stayed in street clothes without stepping on the floor for Washington. Until Wednesday.
In a 128-116 win over the Bucks, Davis reminded everyone just how good he is, going for 34 points, 12 rebounds, four assists, two steals and a block. He made 11 of 20 shots and hit a 3-pointer. Best of all, he played 34 minutes. Yes, it was against the Bucks, who figure to be awful this season, but AD didn't make the schedule and knocking the rust off against Milwaukee isn't the worst thing given how long it's been since he played. Since arriving in Washington, Davis has been a popular trade candidate in rumors and whispers around the league. The Wizards have insisted they are not interested in moving him, despite putting contract extension negotiations on hold this summer. It's hard to blame the organization for wanting to see how he fits first -- and how much he'll even be available -- before committing big money to him. Davis's talent is undeniable, but he'll be 34 in March and a litany of injuries over the course of his career has repeatedly kept him on the sidelines. He's played 56 games or fewer in six of the last 10 seasons.  But hey, at least he was out there on Wednesday, playing with Trae Young and the Wizards. The crowd seemed to appreciate it. 
You know the old saying, "smoke 'em if you got 'em?" This was the "chant it while he's actually playing" basketball equivalent. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Ja Morant: AWhen the Trail Blazers traded for Morant, the nearly universal question became "how is that going to work?" In the opener, the answer was "pretty well."According to a report in The Athletic in early October, new Blazers coach Micah Nori didn't believe it made sense to start Damian Lillard and Morant in the same backcourt. That thinking didn't even last through the first game. 
The Blazers started Morant on Wednesday in a runaway 124-83 home win over the Suns. In 23 minutes, Morant went for 14 points (on 6-for-8 shooting), five rebounds, eight assists and three steals with just one turnover. It's the smallest of sample sizes, but the Blazers will obviously take it. The main concern with adding Morant was that Portland already had an overcrowded backcourt with Lillard, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson and Shaedon Sharpe (who is expected to miss extended time with a knee injury). The situation was further complicated by the Blazers unlocking Deni Avdija last season and realizing the team worked better when the offense ran through him. Throwing another high-usage player like Morant into the mix seemed inadvisable, especially when he's used to having the ball in his hands and isn't a good shooter (31.1% from deep for his career). Against the Suns, Morant hit a pair of threes. Even more encouraging, he showed the kind of effort the Blazers will need from him if this odd mix is going to work over the course of a long season.

title: Lions' Sam LaPorta voices displeasure about contract situation - CBS Sports
description: LaPorta is not a happy camper right now
body:
LaPorta is not a happy camper right now
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:21 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Sam LaPorta is taking a unique approach in terms of his contract situation. Instead of keeping things in-house, LaPorta has chosen to publicly voice his displeasure. A former Pro Bowler, LaPorta is in the final year of his four-year, $9.47 million rookie contract. He is slated to earn $5.78 million in cash earnings this season. LaPorta, based on his comments, is clearly not happy that he has yet to receive a contract extension from the Lions. "I think the combination of like getting your heartstrings twisted, as well as the violent sport that we play, you know, it sucks and it's disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt," LaPorta said on Pardon My Take. "You know, like last year, whatever it was week nine, week 10. I break my f-----g back for the team, and then I'm going out there this year, and I'm balling, and maybe they're not showing the love. "Yeah, it sucks. I'm going to continue to be a pro, and you know, I just a lot of that to my agent, and he handles that great. ... So I'm going to continue to go do my thing and ball out. And in three months, if I don't get to wear the Honolulu blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's gonna be all good. Yeah, I'll get paid somewhere else. So whatever." 
As he alluded to, LaPorta will likely have a big payday this offseason, whether it's with the Lions or someone else. His current market value is a three-year, $45.1 million deal, according to Spotrac. A former second-round pick, LaPorta has been a valuable part of the Lions' offense since he was drafted back in 2023. He made the Pro Bowl as a rookie and has caught 213 passes and 23 touchdowns in 47 regular season games. During the Lions' 2023 playoff run, he caught 21 of 27 targets for 176 yards and a score. LaPorta has bounced back this season after a serious back injury sidelined him for the second half of the 2025 campaign. He's been especially good over the past two games; he caught eight passes for 84 yards and a touchdown against the Panthers in Week 5 and caught each of his five targets for 88 yards and a score during last week's win over the Cardinals. It's very possible that the Lions -- and other potential teams that might be interested in his services -- are turned off by his decision to be so vocal about his contract status, especially with the Lions getting ready for a big showdown against the rival Packers. 
Talent, however, usually tops anything else in the NFL. As long as LaPorta continues to produce, he will surely have a robust market if he becomes a free agent this offseason. He has certainly made it clear that he is comfortable with the prospect of becoming a free agent for the first time this offseason if he and the Lions do not come to terms on a long-term deal.

title: Kristaps Porziņģis trade destinations: Three viable moves the Warriors could make - CBS Sports
description: Porziņģis is out indefinitely and could walk away from the game, but the Warriors could still find a way to move
body:
Porziņģis is out indefinitely and could walk away from the game, but the Warriors could still find a way to move him
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        There's no such thing as an untradable player in the NBA. As frequently as we call contracts immovable, it's worth remembering that Russell Westbrook once changed teams in all five seasons of a supermax contract. Proximity to retirement isn't necessarily an impediment either. In 2007, the Dallas Mavericks managed to sign-and-trade Keith Van Horn roughly eight months after he played his final NBA game because they needed some filler salary to complete their Jason Kidd blockbuster. If a team wants to trade a player badly enough, there's almost always a way to do so.Still, the Golden State Warriors are facing an uphill climb to move Kristaps Porziņģis, at least for now. On Wednesday, ESPN reported that the Warriors are exploring possible deals involving their high-profile center, but for a variety of reasons, he is an enormously tricky player to trade right now:Porziņģis has been dealing with POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome) over the past two seasons, and is considering stepping away from basketball for good. At the very least, availability concerns mean he has no positive trade value as a player right now. Any team considering acquiring him would have to view any future on-court value as merely a bonus.When they re-signed Porziņģis this offseason, the Warriors gave him a $3 million guarantee for the 2027-28 season. This is by no means an enormous figure, but in the apron era, every cent counts. No team is going to be eager to pay Porziņģis $3 million not to play for them, making him a bit more cumbersome than a traditional expiring contract. Frankly, this was a bizarre own goal on Golden State's part. One potential path for Golden State's 2027 offseason is near-max cap space, and considering Porziņģis would have needed to pass a physical with another team in order to leave, it's just hard to imagine he had the leverage to demand any sort of 2027-28 guarantee. That is especially true considering the Warriors are paying him $20 million this season, far above the mid-level exceptions most other teams had to potentially offer him.By virtue of using the taxpayer mid-level exception on De'Anthony Melton, the Warriors are hard-capped at the second apron. They only have around $350,000 in room beneath it right now, meaning Golden State lacks the wiggle room to take on a bigger salary than Porziņģis without adding other players.A good chunk of the NBA is not eligible to be traded right now. Most 2026 free agents are not tradable until Dec. 15, with a handful having to wait until Jan. 15 instead. Porziņģis notably avoids that fate because the Warriors managed to sneak his deal in right before the beginning of free agency, allowing them to structure it as an extension that did not include a raise big enough to trigger a six-month trade restriction. He can be moved right now, but many other players who might factor into a deal like this, including seven of his teammates, cannot.
        
            
                Warriors exploring trades for Kristaps Porziņģis, who is contemplating future amid health issues, per report
                
                    Robby Kalland                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Put all of this together and you have an enormously inconvenient set of trade circumstances. The Warriors, with Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody also sidelined, are starting the season with almost $90 million in salary sitting out due to injuries that preceded this season. Part of their motivation in exploring a Porziņģis trade would likely be to salvage this season. If they have to wait until Dec. 15 for the right combination of players to become tradable, it might be too late. At best, Porziņģis is essentially just matching money from a trade perspective. At worst, he's someone they'll have to attach something to in order to move.
So, are there any viable moves out there? A few come to mind.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Milwaukee BucksThe best version of Golden State's roster is pretty dependent on having centers that can shoot. As the Warriors learned with Jonathan Kuminga, pairing a third shaky 3-point shooter with Butler and Draymond Green tends to compromise their spacing. Green can play center when needed, but at this point shouldn't do so on a full-time basis. And while Al Horford is here, he's 40 and not equipped for a starter's workload. This was the theoretical purpose of the Porziņģis acquisition. Golden State needs tall people who can make 3s, especially now that Quinten Post is gone.The only starting-caliber shooting center available at what would probably be a reasonable price is Myles Turner. The Milwaukee Bucks signed him in a last-ditch effort to keep Giannis Antetokounmpo. It didn't work. Turner had a bad year and has three expensive seasons left on his contract. With Kel'El Ware needing minutes to potentially grow into Milwaukee's long-term center, swapping out Turner for a shorter Porziņģis contract and Moody (needed for money-matching purposes) makes plenty of sense. 
The Bucks don't even have to worry about Porziņģis' health knocking them into the relegation zone because they don't control their own first-round pick. A team like Milwaukee, with no short-term stakes, is the ideal landing spot for Porziņģis. If he can come back down the line, great, he'd be a nice backup. If they have to cut him, well, it's not as though they needed that wiggle room anyway.
There's one pretty substantial hiccup here, though, and it's the remaining years left on Turner's contract. Adding him more or less takes max-level cap space off the table for the Warriors next summer. The question then becomes, how valuable is that option, really? Nikola Jokić and Antetokounmpo are technically slated for unrestricted free agency... but does anyone really doubt that they'll re-sign with their current teams? Even if they don't, why would they pick the aging Warriors? Karl-Anthony Towns can opt out of his contract in New York, but he's made it clear he wants to be a Knick for life. Odds are, something gets done there. Difference-makers just don't change teams through free agency anymore.Besides, preserving that cap space means renouncing their rights on their own free agents. Maybe Green takes a discount to stay for sentimental reasons. Butler has never shown a willingness to do that. Adding Turner robs the Warriors of upside over the next few years, but it's not as though Golden State really had much of it to begin with. What's the goal here? Are they genuinely trying to win a title? Or just trying to allow Stephen Curry to retire with some dignity? If it's the latter, Turner makes sense.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Charlotte HornetsThe Hornets willingly took a step back this season by trading LaMelo Ball, and ever since, they've been perfectly willing to take on money when it suits them. They got three second-round picks to eat the Dorian Finney-Smith contract, for example, and are more than flexible enough to waive Porziņģis next offseason if needed. If anything, they might prefer to use his inflated cap number and partial guarantee to get more draft capital to take on another bigger contract down the line.
The Hornets are relatively light on high-end talent but stuffed with mid-sized contracts attached to playable NBA veterans. Royce O'Neale could help the Warriors. Grant Williams could help the Warriors. Grayson Allen could help the Warriors, though they already have quite a few shooting guards. If the name of the game here is just "turn salary that isn't playing for us into salary that could play for us," Charlotte is a pretty easy fit. Of the three, Williams has the only expiring deal, but O'Neale has the lowest cap figure.The Warriors have three tradable second-round picks. Is that enough to make a deal like this happen? Maybe, depending on who the Hornets are sending out. Charlotte might want to see how its rotation shakes out over the first few weeks before landing on who, if anyone, it would want to trade. First-round capital, even a swap, just doesn't make sense in a deal this small, so it's either seconds or bust.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New Orleans PelicansThe Pelicans are mostly a placeholder for the concept of using Porziņģis' salary plus draft picks to trade for a very good player. The Warriors have, at times, been linked to both Trey Murphy and Herb Jones. The Pelicans, having re-signed Saddiq Bey to a three-year extension, may elect to move one of their other wings to eventually give him a starting job. Jones, as a shaky shooter, is the worst fit of the two. Murphy, given his scoring and team-friendly contract, would cost far more. Golden State controls most of its own draft capital. The question is how much, if any, actually makes sense to give up in a win-now trade.
Murphy is a very valuable No. 3 option. The Warriors are emphatically not a No. 3 option away from any sort of meaningful winning. If this is the direction the Warriors want to take a Porziņģis trade, it probably has to come with some proof of concept. If Curry can keep Golden State in, say, the race for the top six for a month or two, and Butler looks close to a return, then maybe it makes sense to make a trade involving multiple first-round picks. In the more likely event that the Warriors are more of a Play-In team (or worse), those picks become precious.Curry is still a top-10 player when healthy. He missed half of last season and is nearing the end of his legendary career. Golden State has to balance the upside his mere presence creates with the reality that his window probably closed when Butler tore his ACL last season. Getting better while he's still a star-level player would be nice. This is still, functionally, a rebuilding team, and basically everything would have to go right to justify trading future for present here.

title: Dodgers 'fully expect' Shohei Ohtani to pitch in 2027, and they have three paths to take with two-way star - CBS Sports
description: The Dodgers say Ohtani will not need surgery after nursing two injuries in 2026, and they will have him return to
body:
The Dodgers say Ohtani will not need surgery after nursing two injuries in 2026, and they will have him return to double duty next year
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:06 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Surgery is not on the table for Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani, who played through knee and biceps injuries late in the season and into the postseason, president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman announced Wednesday. The Dodgers expect Ohtani to pitch next season and continue as a two-way player."That's not on the table," Friedman said when asked about Ohtani having surgery. "... I fully expect him to pitch next year. I not only expect him to pitch, we're excited about him pitching."  Ohtani, 32, did not pitch after July 3 due to the knee injury. He nursed the biceps injury throughout the season and it eventually contributed to the team's decision to shut him down as a pitcher. Ohtani threw bullpen sessions and faced hitters in live batting practice to prepare to return to the mound in late August, but he had to be shut down.The injuries clearly hampered Ohtani at the plate late in the year. He spent 15 days on the injured list in September, went 5 for 21 with eight strikeouts in five regular-season games after returning, then went 5 for 26 with 10 strikeouts in the postseason. Ohtani hit .167/.298/.240 with one home run in his final 26 games of 2026, postseason included.
Before the injuries, Ohtani made 14 starts and threw 85 ⅔ innings with a 1.79 ERA and terrific under-the-hood numbers. He has a career 2.83 ERA in 114 regular-season starts. Ohtani has pitched like an ace whenever he's been on the mound, so it's easy to understand why he and the Dodgers continue to pursue it.There are three paths the Dodgers can take with Ohtani as a pitcher in 2027.1. Let him pitch all yearMaintain the status quo, basically. Let Ohtani break camp as a regular member of the rotation and plan on pitching him every sixth day -- the Dodgers employ a full-time six-man rotation -- from Opening Day through the end of the season, which the Dodgers hope is at the end of the World Series. This is surely what Ohtani wants, and, of course, he has say in this matter.Here is the Dodgers rotation depth chart going into next season:RHP Shohei OhtaniRHP Yoshinobu YamamotoLHP Blake SnellRHP Tyler GlasnowRHP Roki SasakiLHP Justin WrobleskiRHP Emmet SheehanRHP Gavin Stone (coming off shoulder surgery)Even if the Dodgers are unable to re-sign Tarik Skubal, there is plenty of depth there to continue with the six-man rotation, and even skip Ohtani's starts now and then to give his body a break. Wrobleski and Sheehan are overqualified as No. 5-6 starters and Stone threw the ball quite well during his minor-league rehab appearances. Los Angeles could always sign a depth starter as well.

        
            
                Who's to blame for Dodgers' shocking NLCS loss vs. Brewers? Five places to point fingers
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
2. Start his season late (on the mound)Because Ohtani qualifies as a two-way player and thus counts against the roster as a position player, the Dodgers are still able to carry the full complement of 13 pitchers. They can slowly build Ohtani up as a pitcher during pregame work while he remains in the lineup as a hitter, then they can insert him into the rotation in, say, June. That could keep him healthiest in the long run.
This is more or less what the Dodgers did with Ohtani as he worked his way back from UCL surgery in 2025. He threw his bullpens and live batting practices in the afternoon, then hit at night. Ohtani made his first start on June 16 and gradually built up from one inning in June to six innings in September. Ohtani then made four starts and threw 20 ⅓ innings in the 2025 playoffs. There is proof of concept here. The Dodgers and Ohtani have done exactly this already.3. Use him as a relieverA fine idea that will be difficult to put into practice. Warming up in the bullpen (or even in the batting cage behind the dugout) would be difficult when Ohtani has to hit in the previous inning, or even if his lineup spot is due up fourth or fifth. Ohtani's lineup spot was eight spots away when he came out of the bullpen for Japan in the 2023 World Baseball Classic Championship Game.
Also, the Dodgers would lose the DH spot once Ohtani comes out of the game as a reliever. MLB's rules allow Ohtani to stay in the game as the DH when he's the starting pitcher, but not as the DH. The Dodgers could get around this by using him as the closer and as their final pitcher of the game. But again, how does he warm up? And if it goes to extra innings, you're down Ohtani's bat.The Dodgers should be good enough to win the NL West next season without a full season of Ohtani the pitcher, so starting him late seems like the best approach. That said, the difference between 15 starts of Ohtani and 23 starts of Ohtani could be the difference between getting a Wild Card Series bye or having to play in that best-of-three series. You want the bye, always.Ohtani just completed Year 3 of his landmark and heavily deferred 10-year, $700 million contract. The injuries and late-season fade at the plate make it nearly certain that Ohtani will not win a fourth consecutive MVP award, and the fifth MVP of his career.

title: College Football Playoff tiers: Miami, Georgia lead contenders at midseason - CBS Sports
description: Sorting the nation's playoff hopefuls into tiers based on résumés, ceilings and remaining paths as we enter the s
body:
Sorting the nation's playoff hopefuls into tiers based on résumés, ceilings and remaining paths as we enter the season's second half
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Validation.As the only CBS Sports voter to have Miami at No. 1 before the season, I'll admit, the Hurricanes climbed to the top spot in the AP poll a few weeks before I expected them to after midseason carnage across the top 25. Miami is one of only six unbeatens left on the board, and it doesn't appear that anyone's safe moving forward during a year of extreme parity in the sport.We're sifting through the AP Top 25 to separate elites from the teams still selling themselves on potential in Week 8. There's a handful of true contenders who have already shown a championship ceiling against quality competition, while others need a large sample size before belonging in that conversation.Reputation gets you attention, but play on the field and execution are what truly qualify in front of the CFP selection committee. Here's where the nation's playoff hopefuls fall in our contender tiers, with championship credentials driving the discussion.Tier A.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Georgia (6-1) The Bulldogs' stock price shouldn't change after their home loss to Auburn. Three turnovers from Gunner Stockton were to blame, and the likelihood that happens again this season is slim. Kirby Smart mentioned after the game that he felt Georgia beat itself, and it's hard to disagree with that. The Bulldogs remain our SEC favorite at midseason and should get to the CFP as a top-4 seed.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Miami (6-0) Survival. That's what it's about for the Hurricanes throughout the duration of the season. Getting past Notre Dame on Nov. 7 is not a necessity, but it would virtually secure a top-4 seed in the bracket and an opening-round bye if they do. We're sticking with the season-long projection that Miami will be the Power Four's lone unbeaten on Selection Sunday and enter the CFP as the No. 1 seed.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Notre Dame (6-1)Winning on the road is never easy. Doing it against a top-10 opponent is even more difficult. Notre Dame showed considerable fight at BYU after trailing 21-10 at halftime before taking a three-point lead in the fourth quarter prior to the Cougars' game-winning drive. The Fighting Irish are a better-executed goal-line play away from being unbeaten and ranked No. 1 in the AP poll, so it would be unwise to dismiss the Irish after one hiccup. That said, a loss to Miami in a couple of weeks severely alters Notre Dame's CFP outlook.
        
            
                Is Notre Dame in danger of missing CFP? Familiar conversation around Irish emerges after first loss of season
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Tier B.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    BYU (6-0) The best of the three unbeatens left in the Big 12, the Cougars catapulted themselves into the spotlight with the win over Notre Dame. Controversial ending aside, BYU earned it against a top-10 opponent with a victory that almost looked personal for Bear Bachmeier and his teammates. Can the Cougars bring that same level of swagger to UCF this weekend as a 6.5-point favorite or during their trip to Utah on Nov. 7? Those are two potential trouble spots for Kalani Sitake's squad.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Indiana (6-1)I wonder how often Curt Cignetti smirks when he reads that this Indiana team isn't as good as his last one. Well, duh. It's hard to replicate a 16-0, record-setting season when you replace a Heisman-winning quarterback and several other top-end playmakers. However, through seven games, the Hoosiers are literally a foot from being unbeaten on a 23-game winning streak entering Saturday's tilt at Michigan. There's still a lot to like about an elite-coached squad that's going to be a tough out in December. Despite the loss to Ohio State, I'm slotting Indiana above the Buckeyes at this point given the injury to Julian Sayin.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kentucky (6-1) Graced with an intellectual at quarterback and a first-year coach who might be the most confident leader in the FBS not named Curt Cignetti, the Wildcats are legit. There were doubts when this team trailed 17-0 at South Carolina and more when they lined up for the win against LSU the following week in overtime, but Will Stein delivers, man. Saturday's victory at Oklahoma might've been this squad's best given the setup -- a road underdog against a team coming off a rivalry victory over Texas in Red River. And Kentucky came through.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Ohio State (6-1) The Buckeyes aren't in that top group because of Sayin's injury, a considerable unknown moving forward this season. It's up to backup Luke Fahey to keep Ohio State on track in the Big Ten picture and CFP conversation, with matchups left to play against USC, Oregon and Northwestern, among others. When you're equipped with Jeremiah Smith and an elite defense, you always have a chance, but the Buckeyes have been downgraded without QB1.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Ole Miss (5-1) Pete Golding got his team's attention during their bye week earlier this month after a loss in Gainesville muddied up the hot start and revealed warts. Ole Miss has looked light years better defensively over the last two weekends, culminating with the Rebels' 28-point swat of Missouri in Week 7. They're a betting underdog Saturday at Texas, still have to play fifth-ranked Georgia and travel to Oklahoma before the Egg Bowl. Trinidad Chambliss, after what he showed during last season's CFP, is a warrior and gives Ole Miss a chance to win every game the rest of the season.Tier C.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Alabama (5-2) Outside of Texas, no team's stock has tanked faster than Alabama's over the last two games. Alabama hasn't scored a second-half point since Oct. 3 when the Crimson Tide humiliated Mississippi State, 56-23. Since then, the offense has been kept in check by Georgia and Tennessee, leading to jeers for Kalen DeBoer and Ryan Grubb. The upcoming showdown at LSU next month could determine the SEC's final at-large CFP entry.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    LSU (5-2) Lane Kiffin's team hasn't exhausted their CFP chances just yet, and they could make a Miami-like impact as a high seed if they get there. The Tigers don't need another reminder of their ceiling. They need to start living there and playing with a better sense of urgency. The overtime loss at Kentucky still stings. However, win the games ahead -- especially Alabama -- and CFP seeding takes care of itself. This defense changes considerably without Princewill Umanmielen, so his return is vital.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tennessee (6-1) Jim Knowles is earning every penny of his $2 million salary as the Vols' defensive coordinator. He has fixed just about every problem that Josh Heupel asked of him, and Tennessee has a chance to win the SEC as a result. Last weekend's performance against Alabama was one of the most notable defensive game plans across the sport this fall as the Vols harassed Keelon Russell throughout. Independent of quarterback questions right now, Tennessee has the defense and run game with DeSean Bishop to make a run.
